samf-junior-2021-r2-03.title: Parallel lines
samf-junior-2021-r2-03.body:
Through the vertex marked $x^\circ$ draw a line parallel to the two given lines. The top part of $x$ equals the alternate angle $26^\circ$. The bottom part equals the alternate angle to the interior angle next to $130^\circ$, which is $180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ$. So $x=26+50=76$.

**Answer: 76**

samf-junior-2021-r2-04.title: Count unit cubes
samf-junior-2021-r2-04.body:
The cube is made of 27 unit cubes. Drilling removes the centre cube of each of the 6 faces and the cube in the very middle: $6+1=7$ cubes. Volume $=27-7=20\text{ cm}^3$.

**Answer: 20**

samf-junior-2021-r2-05.title: Parity argument
samf-junior-2021-r2-05.body:
Every path used by the ant adds 1 to the number of times a vertex is touched, so any vertex that is not A or B must have an even number of used paths, while A and B have an odd number. A and B each have 2 paths, so one path at each must be unused. The two vertices on the upper left and upper right of the middle each have 3 paths, so each must have at least one unused path. Hence at least 2 paths are unused (the path at A and the one at the upper left can coincide, and so can those at B and upper right), so the route has length at most 8. It is achieved by A, lower left, middle, upper left, top, upper right, middle, lower right, B.

**Answer: 8**

samf-junior-2021-r2-06.title: Use the four diagonals
samf-junior-2021-r2-06.body:
The four diagonals through the centre each contain $x$ and a pair of opposite numbers. Opposite pairs are $(1,8),(2,7),(3,6),(4,5)$, each with sum 9. So each diagonal sums to $9+x$. The average is $9+x=25$, so $x=16$.

**Answer: 16**

samf-junior-2021-r2-07.title: List them
samf-junior-2021-r2-07.body:
The squares start $1,4,9,\dots$ and the cubes $1,8,27,\dots$. To contain three cubes the list must reach 27. Up to 27 it contains the squares $1,4,9,16,25$ and the cubes $1,8,27$, so 27 integers suffice and are needed.

**Answer: 27**

samf-junior-2021-r2-08.title: Each notch adds 2 cm
samf-junior-2021-r2-08.body:
The original perimeter is $2(10+15)=50$ cm. Cutting a $1\times1$ square from the edge removes 1 cm of edge and adds 3 cm, a net gain of 2 cm. So the perimeter is $50+12\times2=74$ cm.

**Answer: 74**

samf-junior-2021-r2-09.title: Factor the sum
samf-junior-2021-r2-09.body:
The sum is $n+(n+1)+\dots+(n+4)=5n+10=5(n+2)$. For this to be a perfect square, $n+2$ must be $5$ times a square. The smallest is $n+2=5$, so $n=3$ (sum $=25$).

**Answer: 3**

samf-junior-2021-r2-10.title: Count
samf-junior-2021-r2-10.body:
Removing even numbers leaves the 50 odd numbers. Of these, the multiples of 5 are $5,15,\dots,95$: 10 numbers. $50-10=40$.

**Answer: 40**

samf-junior-2021-r2-10.title: Inclusion-exclusion
samf-junior-2021-r2-10.body:
Numbers divisible by 2 or 5: $50+20-10=60$, so $100-60=40$ are left.

**Answer: 40**

samf-junior-2021-r2-11.title: A factor of 10
samf-junior-2021-r2-11.body:
The product contains both the primes 2 and 5, so it is divisible by 10 and ends in 0.

**Answer: 0**

samf-junior-2021-r2-12.title: Rows and columns
samf-junior-2021-r2-12.body:
Each of the 10 rows needs 9 toothpicks, and each of the 10 columns needs 9 toothpicks. Total $10\times9+10\times9=180$.

**Answer: 180**

samf-junior-2021-r2-13.title: Common factor
samf-junior-2021-r2-13.body:
$y$ divides both 10 and 15, so $y=1$ or $5$. If $y=1$ then $z=15$ does not divide into $xz=6$. So $y=5$, $z=3$, $x=2$, sum $10$.

**Answer: 10**

samf-junior-2021-r2-14.title: Split into two parts
samf-junior-2021-r2-14.body:
The backwards-L shape (right column plus bottom row) has 7, 9, 11 blocks in Figures 1, 2, 3, i.e. $2n+5$ blocks in Figure $n$: $65$ for $n=30$. The diagonal blocks inside number $n+1$: $31$ for $n=30$. Total $65+31=96$.

**Answer: 96**

samf-junior-2021-r2-15.title: Big triangle minus a corner
samf-junior-2021-r2-15.body:
Place the diagonal from the top-left corner of the top square to the bottom-right corner of the bottom row. It spans a width of $12$ (the top square is offset by 4 from the left end) and a height of $16$. The right triangle formed with the right side of the bottom row has area $\frac{12\times16}{2}=96$, but its top part sticks out beside the top square: a $4\times8$ rectangle of area $32$ is not part of the shape. The shaded area is $96-32=64\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: 64**

samf-junior-2021-r2-16.title: Place the 2s
samf-junior-2021-r2-16.body:
The two 2s cannot be adjacent, so their positions are $(1,3)$, $(1,4)$ or $(2,4)$: 3 ways. The digits 0 and 1 fill the other two places in 2 ways. Total $3\times2=6$.

**Answer: 6**

samf-junior-2021-r2-17.title: Totals
samf-junior-2021-r2-17.body:
Total of 10 scores $=800$; total of the remaining 8 is $560$. The two removed sum to $240$, average $120$.

**Answer: 120**

samf-junior-2021-r2-18.title: Factorise
samf-junior-2021-r2-18.body:
$y(x-2)=10$, so $x-2$ is a divisor of 10: $1,2,5,10$ (it must be positive since $y>0$). Then $x=3,4,7,12$ with sum $26$.

**Answer: 26**

samf-junior-2021-r2-19.title: Use a multiplier
samf-junior-2021-r2-19.body:
Let there be $3k$ bananas and $8k$ grapes. Then $\frac{3k-1}{8k}=\frac13$ gives $9k-3=8k$, $k=3$. Grapes: $8\times3=24$.

**Answer: 24**

samf-junior-2021-r2-20.title: Triangle is one sixth
samf-junior-2021-r2-20.body:
The triangle is $\frac16$ of the rectangle. With rectangle width $w$: $\frac12aw=\frac16\cdot48w$, so $a=16$.

**Answer: 16**

samf-junior-2021-r2-21.title: Compare areas
samf-junior-2021-r2-21.body:
The radii cut the half-disc into 6 equal sectors of $30^\circ$, i.e. $\frac1{12}$ of a full circle each. One shaded piece (ring part) has area $\frac1{12}(\pi\cdot2^2-\pi\cdot1^2)=\frac\pi4$; four are shaded: $\pi$. The whole shape has area $\frac12\pi\cdot2^2=2\pi$. So $\frac{\pi}{2\pi}=50\%$.

**Answer: 50**

samf-junior-2021-r2-22.title: Which number must be hidden
samf-junior-2021-r2-22.body:
$210=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7$ is divisible by $1,2,3,5,6$ but not by $4$. So $4$ must be face-down: probability $\frac16$. $a+b=1+6=7$.

**Answer: 7**

samf-junior-2021-r2-23.title: Join to the vertices
samf-junior-2021-r2-23.body:
Join the point to the four vertices. Each side's midpoint splits a triangle into two equal parts, so the regions are paired: with areas $a,b,c,d$ round the figure (small triangles), the opposite regions satisfy $a+d=b+c$ (both equal half the square). Here the three given regions are $16$, $20$, $32$ and the unknown one is opposite $20$: $16+32=20+x$ gives $x=28$.

**Answer: 28**

samf-junior-2021-r2-23.title: Total area
samf-junior-2021-r2-23.body:
Opposite regions sum to the same amount, namely half the area of the square. So $20+x=16+32=48$, and $x=28$.

**Answer: 28**

samf-junior-2021-r2-24.title: Equal distances
samf-junior-2021-r2-24.body:
Let the outward time be $t$ hours: $15t=10(2-t)$, so $25t=20$ and $t=\frac45$ h $=48$ min.

**Answer: 48**

samf-junior-2021-r2-24.title: Time ratio
samf-junior-2021-r2-24.body:
The distances are equal, so times are in the inverse ratio of the speeds, $10:15=2:3$. The 120 minutes split $2:3$ into 48 and 72, and the faster outward leg is the shorter time: $48$ min.

**Answer: 48**

samf-junior-2021-r2-25.title: Cases
samf-junior-2021-r2-25.body:
The six known numbers $4,7,13,15,16,17$ sum to $72$. If $p\le13$ the median is $13$, giving $p=19$, a contradiction. If $13\le p\le15$ the median is $p$: $(72+p)/7=p$ gives $p=12$, a contradiction. If $p\ge15$ the median is $15$: $72+p=105$, $p=33$, which is valid.

**Answer: 33**
